Duplicate invoice detection

Scans your bills and payments for the same bill entered or paid twice, a supplier under two records, and credit notes nobody used, and lists the unpaid duplicates first.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, September under review, scan window 1 July to 31 October. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin duplicate invoice detection skill

Can you check our supplier bills for duplicates? September is the month I care about.

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
  2. Which company? If you have a group, do I also scan across the companies?
  3. Which period do I scan, and how far back before it? Duplicates often cross a month end.
  4. Which suppliers bill the same amount on purpose, such as rent, insurance or software?
  5. Which sensitivity do you want: Strict, Standard or Permissive? If you do not say, I use Standard and a 7-day window.
  6. Do you have results from an earlier scan?

Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading only. Scan 1 July to 31 October around September. Our landlord, our insurer and three software suppliers bill the same every month. Standard is fine. No earlier scan.

The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

Claude

Here is my plan. I scan every bill and payment at Northbrook Trading from 1 July to 31 October. I use Standard sensitivity and a 7-day window. Your landlord, insurer and three software suppliers count as normal repeat billers.

Rule 7 cannot run here. It finds two suppliers that share one bank account, and MosoFin cannot see bank details. Who can check that in your banking system? Shall I start?

The bank's payments team can check it. Yes, go ahead.

Claude

I scanned all 1,284 bills. Five clusters look like duplicates. The exposure leaves out the one bill in each cluster that is real.

Flagged clusters
ClusterExposureWhat I foundConfidence
A$1,250.00Harbor Office Supply INV-0442, entered and paid twiceVery High
B$4,860.00Crestline Logistics INV-7731, paid by cheque and again by ACHHigh
C$3,200.00Pinnacle Design INV-2210, under two supplier records, one bill still openHigh
D$980.00Acme Corp and Acme Corporation, two days apart, name score 0.91Medium
E$950.00Summit Cleaning, 1 Sep and 6 SepMedium

Summit also bills $950 on the 1st of each month. That is a pattern, so only the 6 Sep bill is a suspect.

Claude

D and E are Medium, $1,930 together. They stay on the list, below the headline. Under Strict, the headline is $11,240.

Claude

Most duplicates are honest errors, not fraud. Here is what I propose, unpaid first:

Recovery plan
ActionAmountCluster
Void the open Pinnacle bill before you pay it$3,200.00C
Ask Crestline for a credit, a refund or a set-off$4,860.00B
Ask Harbor for a credit on its next invoice$1,250.00A
Merge the two Pinnacle records and the two Acme recordsC and D

That is $3,200.00 caught before payment and $6,110.00 paid out to recover. A merge is not reversible in most systems, so check each pair first. I void nothing, merge nothing and ask no supplier for money.

Claude

Harbor also owes you money. Credit note CN-0011 for $410.00 is still open, and you paid three later Harbor bills in full. It is not a duplicate, so it is not in the exposure.

Claude

I ran 9 of the 10 rules. Rule 7 did not run, and the bank's payments team owns it. So this scan found the duplicate errors. It does not show that the fraud test passed.
